defects.title: Fixed output paths on ready-today rows (cleanup-audit, index-repo) break WC-11 with no coordinator rule
defects.quote: Two workers in one worktree must never write the same file. Default output paths carry a timestamp or the slug the coordinator passes
defects.what_goes_wrong: Section 3.1 keeps cleanup-audit (fixed .claude-audit/ dir and progress.json, 'one audit per worktree at a time') and index-repo (fixed PROJECT_INDEX.md, brief passes none, fix only 'state the output location') as ready, so two such workers in the default shared worktree overwrite each other, which WC-11 forbids, and neither section 2.3 nor any AC contains the serialization rule the cleanup-audit row cites.
defects.is_fixed_when: Either cleanup-audit and index-repo take a coordinator-passed per-run output path/slug that the brief column and a P1 change require, or section 2.3 (and the brief template) states a coordinator obligation not to run two such Tasks in one worktree, with a check that covers it.
defects.deletion_note: No: deleting WC-11 or relabelling the rows to 'needs change' without giving them a per-run path or a stated serialization rule would hide the clash instead of resolving it (moving them out of 'ready' with a P1 per-run path is a fix).
defects.present_in_others_hint: Section 3.1 rows (cleanup-audit line 85, index-repo line 86), section 2.3 brief contents (line 73), P1 scope (line 159), count 'ready today 10' at line 75; also the coordinator rule for code-writing commands sharing a worktree. Note: init-lite is NOT part of this defect because its brief passes --output <file>.

defects.title: WC-11 default-path rule is not scoped to unattended mode and contradicts SA-1
defects.quote: Default output paths carry a timestamp or the slug the coordinator passes
defects.what_goes_wrong: WC-11's first clause (and WC-10's wait splitting) has no unattended scope, while SA-1 says that without --unattended every output path stays as it is today, so an implementer must guess whether standalone /sc:index-repo etc. get timestamped default names.
defects.is_fixed_when: WC-11 (and every WC rule that changes defaults) states that it applies only under --unattended or to a coordinator-passed path, or section 2.2 carries one sentence scoping WC-2 to WC-12 to unattended runs and SA-1 is cross-referenced.
defects.deletion_note: No: deleting WC-11 would drop the parallel-safe-writes requirement (defect c18-d1); the fix is adding a scope sentence.
defects.present_in_others_hint: WC-10 (line 68) wait splitting, section 2.2 intro (line 54), SA-1 (line 146), SA-3 (line 148).

defects.title: P1 adds --unattended to every 3.1/3.2 command before P2/P4 make it safe or decided
defects.quote: the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate)
defects.what_goes_wrong: After P1 the flag exists on auggie-review, task, post-release, pr-submit and implement while their gate and outward-default resolutions land only in P2 or P4, so /sc:auggie-review <PR> --unattended still posts to the PR (WC-9 violated), AC-1.1 requires an Unattended section on commands whose design waits for D2-D4 (and pr-submit under recommended D3(a) gets no changes), and no P1 check catches it.
defects.is_fixed_when: P1 and AC-1.1 name only the commands whose gate and outward rows are converted in P1 (each later phase adds the flag/section to its own commands), or the spec says the flag on a not-yet-converted gated command refuses to run with status blocked until its phase lands.
defects.deletion_note: Deleting 'every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2' from P1 and AC-1.1 and naming the P1 list is the fix; deleting WC-9 or the per-command rows would not be.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Phase table lines 159-162, AC-1.1 (line 195), section 3.2 phase column for auggie-review/task/post-release/pr-submit/implement, D3 line 240, line 154 ('Phases 1-3 need no user decision'), line 139.

defects.title: E3 skill-direct citation vs section 1.4 'proves the nested route' read as contradiction
defects.quote: so it proves the nested route, not the direct route this spec requires
defects.what_goes_wrong: No wrong outcome: E3 only claims workers invoked /sc:adversarial and it landed as PR #329, and 1.4 qualifies that run as nested-route evidence; no text claims direct-route proof, and no build step or AC depends on the wording (fails test (b)).
defects.present_in_others_hint: INV-A:13 and :35 phrase the skill-direct contract as direct-worker proof, but those are inventory files, not the spec.

defects.title: Troubleshoot 'ready' brief omits the --depth deep short-input STOP that stalls a worker
defects.quote: Under `--unattended`, the `--depth deep` short-input STOP and the `--fix` offer resolve as blocked (P2)
defects.what_goes_wrong: Section 3.1 says troubleshoot runs as a worker now if the brief uses the stated flags, but the stated brief constraint is only 'no --fix', so a brief with --depth deep and a short symptom ends its turn asking a person and stalls with no worker_done until P2 (and --unattended does not exist before P1).
defects.is_fixed_when: The troubleshoot 'Brief must pass' cell (and the P0 brief template) also excludes --depth deep with a short (<10 words) input until the P2 fix, or the row stops calling it ready without that condition.
defects.deletion_note: No: deleting the P2 fix or the STOP mention leaves the stall; the brief condition must be added.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Section 3.1 intro line 79, P0 brief template (line 158), AC-0.4 smoke run (line 194), INV-B:239.

extra_noticed.title: WC-3 optional ask route can make the AC-2.2 gate-trigger run end succeeded
extra_noticed.quote: the session may instead ask the coordinator once
extra_noticed.what_goes_wrong: WC-3 lets a worker session with a preamble ask instead of resolving blocked, but AC-2.2 expects worker_done failed and contract status blocked on every gate-trigger run, so a permitted ask-and-resume path makes the live check fail unless the brief forbids ask (not stated).
extra_noticed.is_fixed_when: AC-2.2 or the section 2.3 brief says the gate-trigger run's brief forbids the ask route (or AC-2.2 accepts the ask-then-answered outcome).
extra_noticed.deletion_note: No: removing WC-3 changes the design; the fix is aligning the check or the brief.
extra_noticed.present_in_others_hint: WC-3 (line 61), AC-2.2 (line 200), section 2.3 (line 73). Raised inside gid 285 (F4, F7), not placed in a defect's gids.
